claims.why: Held back: the most important recent change. Aerocivil, the civil aviation authority, took back the running of the airport on 1 September 2025 and runs it directly; Wikipedia's infobox gives Aeronáutica Civil as operator. OurAirports' home link still points to aerocali.com.co, the former concessionaire's site, while the record's own website field and Wikipedia give aeropuertocali.aerocivil.gov.co. Nothing in the truncated old text to replace. For Andy.

claims.claim: attack on the air traffic radar at Candelaria, 16 September 2026
claims.why: Held back: at about 07:00 on 16 September 2026 drones carrying explosives attacked Aerocivil's 3D air traffic radar at El Carmelo, Candelaria, Valle del Cauca, a radar tied to the airport's operations. No one was hurt; Aerocivil activated contingency procedures to keep air navigation services running in the south west. Bogotá preliminarily blamed the FARC. Sources consulted by El País, cited by Aviacionline, spoke of minor damage without interruption of operations, not confirmed by Aerocivil. No flight disruption at Cali is reported. For Andy to decide.

claims.claim: earthquake of 10 August 2026: brief closure, normal service from that night
claims.why: Held back, for the record: the magnitude 7.4 earthquake of 10 August 2026 (epicentre in Chocó) cut the terminal's power; operations resumed normally that night and Aerocivil reported no damage to the infrastructure or movement areas. Over, so not for the Overview.
